passages.provision_quote: (42) human trafficking of a minor, in violation of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, except, with respect to a violation of paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, where the person who committed the offense was a victim of human trafficking, as described in subdivision (b) or (c) of Section 236.1, at the time of the offense;
passages.note: Authored bill adding one offense to the serious-felony list, including for the Three Strikes Law, with a carve-out for defendants who were themselves trafficking victims.
passages.actor_quote: SB 14, Grove. Serious felonies: human trafficking.

rows.reasoning: SB 14 (2023-2024), authored by Grove and approved September 25, 2023, adds "human trafficking of a minor" to the Penal Code's serious-felony list for all purposes, including the Three Strikes Law. One penalty enhancement for a single offense shows the consequences side of the ladder but does not separate "Breaking the law needs to have real consequences — accountability is the priority." from "Impose the toughest penalties the law allows.", and the bill's own exception for offenders who were themselves trafficking victims cuts against the toughest-penalties rung rather than establishing it.
needs_source: Grove's own words on how the system should respond to lawbreaking in general (questionnaire answer, issue page, or floor statement), to separate the accountability rung from the toughest-penalties rung
Further chair-shaped records in the 2023-2026 term on sentencing or diversion generally, not a single offense category
